meta.title: Who really said "We are going to do for blacks exactly what blacks did for the revolution. By which I mean: nothing"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: No speech, book or interview by Che Guevara is known to contain this line. PolitiFact found no original source; Wikiquote lists it as disputed.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'We are going to do for blacks exactly what blacks did for the revolution. By which I mean: nothing'?
meta.ogDescription: Credited to Che Guevara and pinned to a 1959 speech, but no source has ever been produced. PolitiFact and Wikiquote both flag it as unsourced.

answer.label: Not Che Guevara — no documented source
answer.authorDates: Origin unknown · popularly credited to Che Guevara (1928–1967)
answer.sourceLine: No speech, writing or interview of Guevara has been found that contains this line. Online it is often tied to a 1959 speech or press conference, but PolitiFact found no original source or context ↗, and Wikiquote lists it as disputed: “Unclear origin, no sources” ↗.

source.heading: What the record shows

docMeta.dd: None located: no speech, book, letter or interview
“A 1959 speech or press conference”, per unsourced internet claims reported by PolitiFact
PolitiFact, 17 April 2013: no original source found

source.excerpt: We’re going to do for blacks exactly what blacks did for the revolution. By which I mean: nothing.
trail: Wikiquote ↗ puts “We are going to do for blacks what blacks did for the revolution. By which I mean: nothing.” in its Disputed section with the note “Unclear origin, no sources.”
The Wikiquote talk page ↗ lists the “exactly what blacks did” wording under “Unsourced”. The note opening that section, dated 11 January 2009, asks for “a reliable and precise source”.

PolitiFact (17 April 2013) ↗ checked a Marco Rubio claim and reported that some online sources date the line to a 1959 speech or press conference. PolitiFact “was unable to find an original source or context for the quote.”
Quote Investigator ↗ has no article on Guevara: searching the site for his name returns “Nothing Found.”
source.excerptNote: This is the wording PolitiFact quoted and Wikiquote’s talk page lists as unsourced. Wikiquote’s main page gives a shorter version without “exactly”, and a 2012 congressional press release ends it with “the Cuban revolution”. No version has a documented source.
source.rightsNote: No documented work contains this wording and no author is known, so it has no source text and no publication date to judge copyright by. quotle.info makes no claim about its copyright status.

author.name: Che Guevara
author.heading: The man it’s pinned on
author.metaLine: 1928–1967 · Argentine Marxist revolutionary, physician & guerrilla leader
author.bio: Ernesto “Che” Guevara was an Argentine-born physician, author and guerrilla leader, and a key figure of the Cuban Revolution. His speeches, essays and letters are widely published and archived, but this line has not been traced to any of them. Its real author is unknown.

misattribution.heading: Why it gets pinned on Che
misattribution.intro: The line is usually offered as proof of Guevara’s attitude to race, and it gets repeated as if it were documented. None of the places that repeat it cite a source.

items.why: This is the setting most often claimed online. PolitiFact ↗ looked for it and found no original source or context. It also said the line could not be fully evaluated without that context.

A press release dated 18 January 2012 ↗ quotes it as “We’re going to do for blacks exactly what blacks did for the Cuban revolution. By which I mean: nothing!” and calls it Guevara’s “own words.” It names no speech, date or document.
The PragerU video page ↗ presents the line with only “he said” and gives no date or source.

misattribution.truthLine: Neither the claimed 1959 speech or press conference nor any other source has been produced. Wikiquote ↗ and PolitiFact ↗ both treat it as unsourced, and whoever wrote it is unknown.

context.heading: Why it matters
lead: The line comes up whenever Guevara’s views on race are argued over. In 2013 Senator Marco Rubio’s office included it in the material it sent PolitiFact ↗ to back his claim that Guevara wrote “extensively” about white superiority. PolitiFact rated that claim Mostly False. It found the documented evidence was a passage in The Motorcycle Diaries, not this quote.

PolitiFact also asked historians about the quote. Jonathan Brown of the University of Texas said that “Blacks did do plenty for the revolution,” and noted that Afro-Cuban troops, bodyguards and advisers served with Guevara. UCLA’s Mark Sawyer had offered a reading of the line in a blog post, but he told PolitiFact he was unsure where it came from.
context.detailsSummary: The real evidence is a different text
detailsBody: Guevara’s attitudes toward Black people can be documented from his own published writing, chiefly a Motorcycle Diaries passage that biographer Jon Lee Anderson told PolitiFact reflected “white, especially Argentine, arrogance and condescension.” Using an unsourced one-liner in place of that documented text weakens the argument it is meant to support.
context.pull: PolitiFact “was unable to find an original source or context for the quote.”
